newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea calls N.Korean kidnap claim "preposterous".
newsitem.headline: S.Korea calls N.Korean kidnap claim "preposterous".

text.p: South Korea on Thursday called North Korea's suggestion that Seoul kidnapped one of its top official "preposterous" and said it would step up diplomatic efforts to grant his wish to seek asylum in the South.

"This is a preposterous claim," said a unification ministry spokesman. A diplomatic crisis has erupted over the fate of Hwang Jang-yop, a senior aide to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il now in Seoul's Beijing embassy.
"But such an absurd reaction by the North does not come as a surprise as that has been their usual tactic," spokesman Kang Ho-yang told Reuters.

South Korea's foreign ministry said Hwang, one of 11 secretaries on the powerful secretariat of Pyongyang's ruling Workers' Party, sought asylum at Seoul's embassy in Beijing on Wednesday along with his assistant Kim Dok-hong.
"We will not spare any effort to honour his wishes," Kang said.
The ministry said Hwang was the highest ranking Pyongyang official ever to seek asylum in South Korea, and analysts said his defection indicated cracks in the Stalinist hierarchy.
